presets.name: End-of-lane safety
presets.desc: Inaudible zero-latency ceiling at −3 dBFS: untouched below it, catches only the odd runaway peak
presets.notes: The doc's safety row. threshold is the ceiling with no makeup: what you set is the peak you get

presets.name: In-ear and monitor guard
presets.desc: Clean limiter at −6 dBFS with a calm release on a monitor send: feedback squeals and dropped mics cannot spike the ears
presets.notes: Zero latency matters on in-ears (comb with bone conduction); a soft clip handles the first cycle of a sudden spike

presets.name: Louder lead, PA-safe
presets.desc: +6 dB into a punchy limiter at −3 dBFS: the solo jumps forward, pick attacks kept, the PA never clips
presets.notes: The doc's louder-lead row; envelope and soft clip share the work

presets.name: Loud and clipped
presets.desc: Pure alias-free soft clipping driven +9 dB: a dense, saturated wall for loud live leads and synths
presets.notes: The doc's loud row. Clip style lands up to 1.7 dB under the threshold (down-sampler headroom)

presets.name: Bass peaks, no low-E distortion
presets.desc: Clean limiter with a slow release and LF hold at −4 dBFS: slaps and low notes held without riding the waveform
presets.notes: The doc's bass row: auto release holds over one LF period, so the gain never tracks a 41 Hz cycle

presets.name: Vocal peak ceiling
presets.desc: Clean limiter at −4 dBFS with a 120 ms release after the vocal compressor: screams and plosives held

refs.why: FOH Brian Pomp ends the lead vocal chain on a limiter
refs.source: Vintage King, Brian Pomp FOH interview, 2017

presets.notes: The doc's vocal row. A stage singer's peaks overshoot any compressor's attack: this is the last word

presets.name: Backing tracks, transparent
presets.desc: 2 ms lookahead, true-peak ceiling at −1 dBTP: playback and keys limited with no first-cycle shaping at all
presets.notes: Reports 2 ms of latency: fine for tracks and pads, avoid on a played instrument monitored in ears
